parts.visual:
A lightbulb company invents a bulb that lasts 100 years. If they sell it, everyone buys one, and the company goes bankrupt 10 years later because they have no repeat customers.

The Dark Solution:
1. Planned Obsolescence: The company intentionally engineers the lightbulb to burn out after 1,000 hours, forcing the customer to come back and buy another one.
2. The Variations: It can be physical (the battery dies), software (the phone won't run the new update), or psychological (the design looks 'old' next year).
parts.audio: Planned Obsolescence is a controversial business strategy where a product is intentionally designed with an artificially limited useful life, forcing the consumer to become a repeat buyer.

questions.question: A massive tech company glues the batteries inside their laptops, making it impossible to replace them. When the battery naturally degrades after two years, the user is forced to buy an entirely new $1,500 laptop. What is this?
options: Physical Planned Obsolescence. They intentionally removed the ability to repair the device to artificially force a massive repeat purchase.
questions.correct_answer: Physical Planned Obsolescence. They intentionally removed the ability to repair the device to artificially force a massive repeat purchase.
questions.explanation: This strategy drives massive profits, but triggers intense consumer backlash and 'Right to Repair' legislation.

questions.question: Listen to the Fashion Executive. What type of obsolescence is he describing?
questions.tts_text: Our clothes are actually very high quality. But we change the exact shade of the colors and the cut of the collars every six months. If someone wears last year's coat, everyone will instantly know it's old.
options: Psychological (Perceived) Obsolescence. The product works perfectly, but the company uses marketing and design to make the customer feel ashamed to be seen using it.
questions.correct_answer: Psychological (Perceived) Obsolescence. The product works perfectly, but the company uses marketing and design to make the customer feel ashamed to be seen using it.
questions.explanation: This is the foundational business model of the entire fast fashion and luxury goods industry.

questions.question: What is the argument *in favor* of Planned Obsolescence from an economic perspective?
options: It drives innovation and employment. If we built cars that lasted 100 years, auto factories would close, millions would lose their jobs, and we would never invent safer, cleaner engines.
questions.correct_answer: It drives innovation and employment. If we built cars that lasted 100 years, auto factories would close, millions would lose their jobs, and we would never invent safer, cleaner engines.
questions.explanation: Our entire consumer economy is built on a cycle of continuous replacement.

questions.question: How do companies use 'Software' for planned obsolescence?
options: By releasing a massive new operating system that requires more processing power, intentionally making older hardware run so slowly that the user gets frustrated and buys a new device.
questions.correct_answer: By releasing a massive new operating system that requires more processing power, intentionally making older hardware run so slowly that the user gets frustrated and buys a new device.
questions.explanation: Apple faced massive federal lawsuits when it was discovered they were secretly slowing down old iPhones.

When a customer is convinced, that they need an updated product, even though their existing product is working well
Proposed legislation that would require manufacturers to provide consumers with the parts and tools to fix their own devices
A customer who buys again from a company that they have previously purchased from
